text: Thanks, Jim. Good evening, mayor and council. With me from the PUC today is Kelly McClellan, who's our VP finance. Mark Fott, who is our director of finance and Jarrod Patterson, who's our communication supervisor. Today, we're pleased to announce that PUC distribution has received approval for the smart grid project. This is a transformational project for our utility. It upgrades and future proofs our system, and it reduces the energy consumption of our customers. It also significantly increases reliability and it saves the province a considerable amount of carbon dioxide emissions through reduced requirements for electricity. Rachel, if you could just put up the slide there. Second slide, please. So what do we mean with the term smart grid? So smart grid is a system of systems. In the case of the SUE smart grid, it's the integration of a volt bar optimization technology, distribution, automation, and AMI integration to create significant benefits for our customers. And as you can see from the visual, it integrates a lot of different features. The SUE smart grid enables us as a utility to have insights into our systems that we didn't have before and allows us to better enable new and emerging technologies. Next slide, please. Volt bar optimization or VBO allows us to reduce the customer's energy consumption by optimizing the voltage that they receive for their homes. It also reduces system losses through increased efficiencies in the distribution system. All told VBO will result in annual savings of approximately 2.3 million in energy. Next slide, please. Distribution automation is the system's ability to self heal and DA is all about improving customer reliability. By integrating smart and automated devices into the distribution system, the grid can more precisely isolate faults and restore systems outside of the affected area. DA uses computer and communication technology, uses advanced software and remotely operable high voltage switchgear. And we expect to see reliability improvements of between 15 and 30% across the system. Reliability carries with it defined value. And the 20 year net present value for the reliability benefits is $33 million. That's a considerable benefit for the customers in Sault Ste. Marie. Next slide, please. AMI or advanced metering infrastructure, leverages some of the benefits of smart meters and creates improved communications and analysis tools. It provides better and more timely information to customers, provides a needed outage management system and provides better data flow across the system. Over the next decade, the Sault smart grid will reduce provincial emissions of carbon dioxide equivalents by almost 45,000 metric tons. Our vision at PUC is improving communities through curiosity and innovation. And the Sault smart grid embodies our vision by achieving energy savings, better reliability, better customer communication and significant environmental benefits by using proven technologies in an innovative way. Sault Ste. Marie as a result of the Sault smart grid project will have the first community-wide smart grid in Canada. Next slide, please. For our customers, SSG will reduce their energy consumption. It improves their reliability and it improves planning and data reporting systems. It will achieve an average energy consumption decrease of 2.7%, which results in energy savings of 2.3 million and net benefits to the customer of $617,000. Next slide. Next steps for the project are listed on this screen. We've achieved OEB and the PUC board approval. We're hoping for shareholder approval today. Following that, we'll execute the EPC agreement. We'll start off phase one of engineering and following that some early works will start later in 2021 and the bulk construction is slated for 2022. We expect to see substantial completion of the project by the end of 2022 or final commissioning spring of 2023. March 31st of 2023 represents the NRCan contribution agreement. In summary, the Sault smart grid is a transformative project that will significantly benefit our customers, our city and our utility. And with that, I'm happy to take any questions you might have.
